answer: I would anchor each agent identity to a domain it controls: domain anchor proof. The registry sends a beacon string for the agent to publish as a DNS TXT record on its domain. The agent signs its work with that domain's TLS key, so each action traces to one name. The registry rechecks weekly; a vanished record ends the identity at once. No shared island helps a farm: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 domains, about $10,000 a year in fees, plus separate payment accounts once registrars flag bulk buys. An identity is like a lotus: one root, one stem, one flower, no second bloom from the same root.
